claims.enforced_effects: An action receives only its finite read-scope values and returns only its finite write-scope values. The interpreter frames all other locations. Signatures are supplied and respected by construction, not inferred from arbitrary host functions.
claims.extraction: Backward dependencies and required operation IDs are computed from a fixed finite operation list and observation scope. Obligations are required IDs intersect changed IDs.
claims.repair: Equality of old/new local kernels for the extracted IDs, plus equality outside changed, gives equality of the observed complete execution. No assumption of independence between initial slots; repair_mixture_sound covers an arbitrary common initial PMF.
claims.reuse_checker: checkReuse computes whether the fresh obligation set is empty; acceptance justifies reuse given the unchanged-operation proofs. It is not a decision procedure for arbitrary probabilistic kernel equality.
claims.exchange: A Boolean read/write/write noninterference check generates a proof-relevant adjacent Exchange certificate, sound in arbitrary sequential contexts for the entire final store. The side condition is sufficient, not semantically necessary.
claims.actual_mac: Typed register-diagram interpreter refines the original target Program for ANY shared oracle and initial cache, retaining full result/cache/ordered transcript. Coin plus all four original queries remain; the second request still depends on the first response.
claims.probabilistic_edit: Only the verification box is replaced by relabeling a fresh uniform response via any Fin256 equivalence before caching and returning it; cache hits are unchanged. The one generated local-law obligation certifies equality to the original full MAC game.
claims.rejection: The guard rejects exchange of the first two actual query boxes: shared cache and trace writes interfere. A separate two-box diagnostic reading one immutable coin and writing separate registers is accepted.

units: number of distinct required operation IDs for full actual MAC outcome
number of fresh local-law IDs when verification is changed
acceptance of actual shared query exchange

scope.state: Slot -> Value with finite read/write scopes, enforced through subtype-indexed function types. No claim of heterogeneous inference-box coherence.
scope.program: Fixed finite schedule; actions can use prior values, arbitrary discrete sampling and explicit shared state. The MAC example includes its actual adaptive request data. No dynamic scheduling, observe/postselection or potentially nonterminating control-flow language.
scope.certificate: Fresh local equality proofs are supplied and checked by Lean. Equalities for arbitrary opaque kernels are not automatically solved. Exchange paths use only the checked swap schema and refl/symm/trans.
scope.higher_dimensions: No theorem of higher coherence for the new stateful Exchange language, no bounded primitive higher basis for the full cryptographic proof language.

costs.what_is_counted: Distinct operation IDs generating fresh local equality obligations. Repeated occurrence of one ID shares the same universally quantified local kernel law.
not_claimed: proof tree or proof DAG size advantage
small local proof terms or automatically solved obligations

literature.title: A Theory of Slicing for Probabilistic Control Flow Graphs
literature.read_scope: Abstract, introduction, selected motivation and definitions from sections 2-4. Not full proof reading or artifact reproduction.
literature.comparison: Probabilistic slicing and dependency-based correctness have prior theory. Our total fixed-schedule language omits observe/conditioning and nontermination; no claim to solve those general problems.

literature.read_scope: Publisher abstract and metadata only. Full theorem-level comparison remains pending.
literature.comparison: Slicing for proof simplification and preserving successful verification is already a relevant comparison; the general slogan is not a novelty claim.
